paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Job can't find God anywhere, east, west, north or south, and he says so out loud. But he doesn't stop talking to Him. He says, "Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold" (Job 23:10). Feeling like God is hard to find is not the same as God being gone, and this passage lets Job say so honestly.

Job also doesn't paint a pretty picture of his pain. He says he is terrified and that thick darkness covers his face, and then adds, "Yet I am not silenced by the darkness" (Job 23:15-17). He looks at a world where the poor groan while "God charges no one with wrongdoing" (Job 24:12), and he asks why. I think the Bible keeps his questions because God can handle them. You can bring Him your hard questions too, and you don't have to dress them up first.

Then Job holds onto something. Even while he's confused, he says God's eyes are on the ways of the mighty, and that their moment is short (Job 24:22-24). So if you're in a dark stretch right now, friend, keep treasuring His words and keep talking to Him, even when you can't see Him. I spent years in the dark myself, and I can tell you that being unseen is not the same as being forgotten. And this story is still in the oven, so there's more to come.
